text: This may be related to dry skin or eczema. Moisturise daily, avoid harsh soaps and see a doctor if it spreads.
If you have eczema, gentle moisturising can help. Please see a doctor if the skin cracks or oozes.
Possible causes include contact with an irritant. Avoid the trigger and see a doctor if it does not improve.
Acne often affects the face, chest and back. A dermatologist can help if it leaves scars.
Keep the area clean and avoid scratching. See a doctor if you notice pus, fever or spreading redness.
Do not use cosmetics on irritated skin. Please see a doctor if it lasts more than two weeks.
Moles that change in size, colour or shape should be checked by a doctor soon.
The photo matches a common mole at 52 percent, but this is not a diagnosis. Please see a doctor if the mole is changing.
Sunburn usually settles in a few days. Stay out of the sun and drink water. See a doctor if blisters are widespread.
Dandruff is common and often linked to a dry or oily scalp. A doctor can advise if the scalp is very itchy or red.

It may be acne. Wash the area gently and see a doctor if it leaves scars.
Antifungal creams are commonly used for ringworm, so please ask a doctor which is right for you.
Take care of the skin: keep it moist, avoid scratching, and see a doctor if it worsens.
When you have eczema flares, avoid hot showers. Please see a doctor if it spreads.
